title: THE ASSESSOR WHO KEPT THE DAM STANDING
deck: For eleven years one honest-looking man has signed a safety certificate he knows is false, and the only people who can fix the dam are the ones his lie was meant to protect.
shape: Six scenes across eight weeks: a number that holds still, a seam in the dark, a loan read for its date and a door nobody had used, a price for water, a credit committee that hears the valley first, and a storm measured against a band written beforehand.

scenes.title: A Number That Holds Still
paragraphs: *Harrow Vale, water-board office · Monday, 16:10 · fifty-six days before the storm season*

The regional authority had sent her to audit the valley's flood model, and it was a good model. Illuminara had spent two days inside it the way a locksmith spends an afternoon inside a lock. Rainfall had a spread. Soil had a spread. Only one input sat perfectly still, and it sat above six thousand roofs.

**Illuminara**  
Left buttress, block thirty-one. Eleven years of seam readings, one a month. Mr Prycé, water does not sit that quietly in a hillside. Every other gauge shivers when it rains on the ridge. This one is deaf.
Dovan Prycé set a cup of tea at her elbow before he answered. He was sixty-one, neat and unhurried, a man who had spent his life being the quietest person in rooms where decisions were made.

**Dovan Prycé**  
The gauge is old and the seam is dry. I'd call that a compliment to the grouting. Harrow is a dull dam, Ms Illuminara. Most of my work is writing *satisfactory* in a careful hand.
She had been a court interpreter once, and she still listened for sentences that had been rehearsed. This one had been sanded. *Dull*, he said, gently, like a man closing a door he had oiled himself.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not accusing anyone. I'm asking what the dam would have to look like for that series to be the honest reading. I would like to go and see. Tonight, if you'll lend me the gallery key.
The pause was shorter than half a second. It was not fear. It was the sound of a man deciding which of two truths to offer first.

**Dovan Prycé**  
The light is best at dusk. Take the blue key. I'll follow when I've locked up.
He did not look at the shelf behind his desk, where a bicycle wheel with one spoke missing hung from a nail. She noticed that he did not look.

scenes.title: The Pencil on the Wall
paragraphs: *Harrow Dam, left-buttress gallery, block 31 · the same evening, 19:40*

Concrete is a record of weight. Illuminara laid her palm flat on the gallery wall and read it as a set of roads along which force travelled, and a few places where the roads disagreed. At block thirty-one one road forked that should not have forked. Load was slipping sideways through a seam no thicker than a pencil line, and under her hand the seam was not still.
*Interpretation*, she told herself. *Not evidence. Test it.*

The official crack gauge, a brass tell-tale glued across the seam, had been painted over, scale and all, in fresh municipal green. Beside it, at knee height, a ruler was pinned to the wall with a bicycle spoke bent into a pointer across the crack. Down the plaster ran a column of pencil ticks, each with a date in a small, careful hand. She read them from the bottom. For nine years they crept four-tenths of a millimetre a year. Then the last two winters, a millimetre and a half each. Then, at the top, three ticks in nine days.

**Dovan Prycé**  
You found my spoke.

**Illuminara**  
I found your pencil. It's the most honest record in this valley.
He sat down on a cable drum as though his legs had agreed to something before he had.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Four-tenths I could live beside. Every morning now I come down before the office opens to see whether the pointer has moved, and every morning I decide not to write what it says.

**Illuminara**  
How long, in your judgement?

**Dovan Prycé**  
A seam like this doesn't snap. It stops giving, and on the day it stops it has nothing left to give. Another wet autumn with the melt on top? I wouldn't bet the valley on the second. I wouldn't bet it on the first.

**Illuminara**  
Then why the paint?
He laughed once, at himself.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Eleven years ago I was the junior assessor. Old Ketteridge wrote a margin note on this block: *requires attention*. Aldermere read it as *unsafe*, because their covenant has a trigger and that was the word that pulled it. They called the loan in thirty days. The Works shut. Two thousand two hundred people left in one winter and I helped load the vans. The next certificate said *satisfactory, with monitoring* in my hand, and I have been monitoring ever since. Your honesty is paid for out of other people's houses. Show me a repair nobody has to lose a job for, or admit you will do what I did, later, with more witnesses.
It was a good objection, and Illuminara did not hurry past it. Behind him, in the dark of the gallery, water ticked in a drain, loud as a clock.

**Illuminara**  
I don't have the repair. I have two facts, and neither is a verdict yet: the seam is moving, and for eleven years you were the only person who knew. So here is what I can promise, and where it stops. Tonight I report nothing. Nothing with your name on it leaves this gallery, and nothing about the dam goes to the lender or the town, until there is a plan with room for you in it. But I won't leave the seam to your pencil, or to mine. Sunniva Achterberg lays a fibre-optic cable across block thirty-one at first light, so that we argue with a measurement and not with me. I read force, Mr Prycé, and I can be wrong. And teach me the valley's money first.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Then give the promise an end, and I'll give you the number. Water on the downstream face of that block. Or fifteen hundredths of a millimetre across the crack in six hours. That is what I have been afraid of since the second winter. A seam that does that is not creeping any more.

**Illuminara**  
Then that is the line, and you drew it, not I. Until the cable is live, the spoke is read on the hour, by you and by me in turn, each figure written under the last, and the same line holds for the spoke as for the cable. If the cable crosses it, or I see water on that face, the week is over that hour. I ring the regional emergency line, the evacuation plan opens, and you hear it from me first. What you tell the board about eleven years is yours to choose. Whether people are warned if the seam goes is not. Inside that line I am asking you for a week.
He took the bent spoke between two fingers and for a while looked only at his own handwriting.

**Dovan Prycé**  
A week. Come to the house. I've a great deal of paper.

scenes.title: The Word and the Date
paragraphs: *Prycé's kitchen, Harrow Vale · the same night, 01:20*

The loan agreement lay open on the kitchen table, a stack as thick as a brick, eleven years of his pencil in the margins. He taught her the valley's money the way a man teaches a language he has had to speak alone. At clause fourteen point three his voice went flat.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Dam Condition Event. If the licensing assessor certifies the dam Class D, unsafe, the lender may call the facility within thirty days. That is the whole trap. It doesn't matter what the repair costs. It matters that I sign the word.
A trap, Illuminara thought, is built to catch one particular animal. She followed the sentence to its end, where a subordinate clause lay in its own shade.

**Illuminara**  
*Unless, at the date of such certificate, a Remedial Programme approved by the Lender's Engineer is then in progress.* Have you read that?

**Dovan Prycé**  
Many times. To have a programme approved, someone must disclose the defect to the lender. It's a locked room, and the key is the same word.

**Illuminara**  
Who discloses? Not you. You are the assessor; you certify. The Borrower discloses. Read me fourteen point five.
He turned to the riders at the back and stopped at one he had not opened in years.

**Dovan Prycé**  
*The Borrower may give written notice of a suspected condition. The Credit Officer may grant a standstill of up to ninety days for the Lender's Engineer to review a remedial programme. No such notice is a certificate or an admission as to classification, and no default is waived.*
He looked at the date on the rider. It was the winter after the Works shut.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Aldermere wrote that door themselves, after the vans. It is addressed to the Borrower, and I have never been the Borrower, so I filed it under administrative.

**Illuminara**  
Then the word was never the key, and it was never the lock. It's the date. Fourteen point three asks what is happening on the day you certify, not what was said before it. So the order matters more than the courage. Voss gives notice under fourteen point five. Halloran grants the standstill. Aldermere's engineer reads a cable and approves a programme. Only then do you certify, and not an hour before. Certify first, and the proviso never attaches.

**Dovan Prycé**  
And until then the seam keeps moving.
He turned pages. The Works Director, *for inspection, maintenance or safety*, could lower the reservoir by up to twelve metres without notice to anyone.

**Illuminara**  
Thrust on a seam goes with the square of the depth. Harrow holds thirty-eight metres at full pool. Take off eleven and the push on block thirty-one is about half. A drawdown is not a programme, and the lender would be right to refuse to call it one. It is what keeps the seam alive for the days the paper takes.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Eleven metres is thirty-three million cubic metres. The Works would be pouring its own stock down the river for nothing.

**Illuminara**  
Not for nothing, if somebody downstream wants it. Who is short of water in the autumn?

He opened his mouth to say *no one*, and closed it. The terraces: four thousand hectares of orchard and winter wheat, and the off-stream reservoirs that Corrin Aske's irrigation union filled every March at pumping prices.

**Illuminara**  
Then let him bite a price off it. The draw must be slow, no more than a quarter of a metre a day, or the wet shoulders of the valley slump into the pool. That is forty-four days. You have fifty-six. Start on Thursday, or the arithmetic runs out before the water does.
Prycé sat quietly for some time. Outside, somebody's dog barked at nothing.

**Dovan Prycé**  
You've left out the strongest thing against you, and I noticed. Even if the lender permits the programme, I have certified *satisfactory* eleven times. That is misrepresentation, a default in its own right whatever the dam is doing. The proviso protects a man who is late. It doesn't protect a liar.

**Illuminara**  
No, it doesn't. That one is yours to answer, and I can't answer it for you. But you are the one who has to stand.

**Dovan Prycé**  
And the people below?

**Illuminara**  
They hear what you know on the day the lender does, and they hear the rest from you before anyone discusses your name.
Every hour until the grey came up, one of them went down the lane to the gallery, read the bent spoke against its ruler and wrote the figure under the last one. It did not move.

scenes.title: What the Water Is Worth
paragraphs: *Tarn Works, director's office · Wednesday, 07:30*
Marguerite Voss listened to all of it standing, with her coat still on, which in Harrow Vale was a form of courtesy. When Prycé had finished she did not look at Illuminara. She looked at him.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Eleven years I have signed for a dam I could not see inside, on the word of a man I trusted with my children's school.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Yes.

**Marguerite Voss**  
I'd have done the same in your chair, which is why I can throw this chair at you. You will say it to the board yourself, Dovan, in your own words, and you won't hide behind the crack. Those are my terms. I'll sign the maintenance order for the low gates myself: dawn, Thursday. And I'll sign the notice to Aldermere under fourteen point five, as Borrower: a suspected condition, independently measured, and the assessor to give his own account in person on Monday. Your name isn't on it. It's true, and the rest is yours to say.

**Dovan Prycé**  
It's a true sentence. I'll say the rest.

Sunniva Achterberg had driven through the night with a drum of fibre-optic cable in the back of a hatchback and spent the day lying on a gallery floor. She put a printout on the desk. It sat inside the line Prycé had drawn in the gallery, and not by much.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Point three one of a millimetre across block thirty-one in eighteen hours. That is faster than your pencil, Mr Prycé. Yesterday I'd have said dull. Today I'll say it's the tail of something. Take eleven metres off and my model gives the margin back. I'll sign *safer*, measured. I won't sign *safe*. I've never seen that word survive a spring.

**Marguerite Voss**  
The water pays a third of stage one: twenty-two anchors in blocks twenty-nine to thirty-three. Halloran can release a first tranche on his own signature, up to a line, and I've priced stage one to sit under it. The notice reaches Aldermere at nine on Thursday, and at the same hour a bulletin goes on every door in the valley: the seam, the pool coming down, a public meeting on Monday. The lender won't hear one word the valley hasn't.
Corrin Aske arrived at noon in his boots and listened with a silence that grew more dangerous as it went.

**Corrin Aske**  
You want me to buy your fear.

**Marguerite Voss**  
I want you to buy thirty-three million cubic metres for the terraces at nine cents against the nineteen it costs you to pump.

**Corrin Aske**  
At nine. In my reservoirs by Christmas, not March, with a written guarantee you can't take back. And a seat on the dam safety panel. My people sleep below that wall too. If you want me to sleep, I read the cable myself. I don't hear about it.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Done. The seat, and the guarantee.

**Corrin Aske**  
And him?

**Dovan Prycé**  
I'll answer for the certificates. I'm not asking you to like it.

**Corrin Aske**  
Good. I don't.

scenes.title: Residents First
paragraphs: *Harrow town hall, Aldermere's credit committee on the screen · the following Monday, 15:00*

Teodor Halloran appeared on the screen with a printed agenda in his hand, a careful man with a careful tie. He had granted the standstill on Thursday. Imre Dalca, Aldermere's engineer, had spent Friday reading Achterberg's cable himself and had approved stage one of the programme at nine that morning. The hall was full, and Illuminara said nothing.

**Teodor Halloran**  
This is a credit review. Item one is covenant compliance.

**Anneke Rowe**  
Item one is me. I nurse at the clinic nine hundred metres below the toe of that dam, and my sons' school is on the flat beside it. Before anyone talks about a loan, tell me whether my children can sleep.

**Teodor Halloran**  
Ms Rowe, with respect, this is a lender's—

**Anneke Rowe**  
With respect, I'll hear it first or I'll hear nothing.
Dovan Prycé stood. His notes shook once and then did not. He had practised, Illuminara thought, for eleven years, in a mirror she had never seen.

**Dovan Prycé**  
For eleven years I certified Harrow Dam *satisfactory, with monitoring*. It was not. Block thirty-one has a seam moving faster each winter, and I hid the rate. Since Thursday the pool has been lowered one point one metres, and an independent cable shows the movement has slowed by a fifth. Mr Dalca has approved stage one of a remedial programme, and so, at three o'clock, as licensing assessor, I classify Harrow Dam Class D at full pool. Ms Rowe, I will not tell you the school is safe. Ilse Bram's flood unit reran the breach map on Friday. At full pool, a breach of block thirty-one puts four metres of water on your flat in eleven minutes. At the pool we will hold by storm season, about half a metre in forty. That is a different flood. It is not no flood. If the cable shows more than fifteen hundredths of a millimetre in six hours, or the pool passes thirty-one metres, the sirens sound and the flat is cleared, whatever the sky is doing. I am the reason you had to ask.
Anneke Rowe said nothing for a while.

**Anneke Rowe**  
Forty minutes is a wish if it's one road and six hundred children. The flat clears in twenty-five or I want a second road. And the clinic goes on the radio net the same hour as the gallery.

**Dovan Prycé**  
The radio I can put in the plan myself. The stopwatch at Wednesday's siren test is yours.
She sat down, which in that room was a verdict of its own.

**Anneke Rowe**  
Wednesday, and I'll stand under the siren myself. Go on. Say the rest to him.

**Teodor Halloran**  
Mr Prycé, you have just told me you falsified eleven certificates, and my committee's first instinct will be to call the loan. My standstill covers the condition. It waives nothing. A committee will ask whether a programme was in progress on the date of your certificate, and whether *approved* means *funded*. Mr Dalca approved stage one at nine, I released the first tranche at ten on my own signature, and you certified at three. I have minuted that order. Had you certified on Thursday, I would be telling you the proviso never attached.

**Dovan Prycé**  
I know. I was made to wait.
Halloran looked, for the first time, at the woman sitting beside the assessor.

**Teodor Halloran**  
And you are?

**Illuminara**  
Someone who was sent to check a flood model. One number, if I may: if Aldermere called the facility today, on a dam with a moving seam, a valley to evacuate and a Works shut down, what does the collateral fetch?

**Teodor Halloran**  
A very small number.
He looked at the figure on his own screen for longer than a man looks who has already decided.

**Teodor Halloran**  
I can't waive a misrepresentation; that belongs to committee. I can refer it with the standstill running and a recommendation that includes that number. I'll record the facility as under active remediation, not unsafe. Mr Prycé's certificates stay reserved, the committee will rule within ninety days, and I would find a lawyer.

**Dovan Prycé**  
I have one. I should have taken her advice some years ago.

scenes.title: Holding
paragraphs: *Harrow Dam, crest · forty-nine days later, 02:10*

The first storm of the season came off the ridge like a door thrown open. Four hundred millimetres in two days. The pool rose two point four metres in the night, and it had eleven metres of empty valley to rise into. Twenty-two anchors, drilled into blocks twenty-nine to thirty-three, held the seam in a grip it had not known since the dam was young.

Before the rain, Achterberg had written three lines on a card and taped it above the gallery radio. At a rise of two point four metres the seam would open by no more than six hundredths of a millimetre. Past the line Prycé had drawn in the gallery, the sirens would sound. At the top of every hour Aske's night man read the cable aloud over the radio. By midnight, one hundredth. By one, two. At two, three.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Forty-four days of drawdown. The Works carrying new debt for ten years. Eleven families gone since September, who'd have gone anyway, they tell me, though I have never found that comfort. I'm out on the thirty-first. The committee will fine me and take my licence. My lawyer says I'll keep my house.

**Illuminara**  
And Ms Rowe?

**Dovan Prycé**  
The boys went to school on the flat on Monday. She timed the siren drill on Wednesday. Twenty-three minutes. She says she still wakes at three. I told her I do as well, and she said good.
Rain hammered the crest. Below them the valley lay dark and unevacuated, six thousand people asleep behind a wall that had, for the first time in eleven years, been described truthfully.
At three the pulse crested, and Achterberg's voice came over the radio from the gallery.

**Sunniva Achterberg (radio)**  
Crest. Four hundredths. Inside the band. The anchor cells rose with the water, so the anchors are carrying it. If the lowered pool had done this alone, they'd have read nothing. Safer, measured. I'll write *safe* on the card when I have seen it survive a spring.

**Dovan Prycé**  
It moved.

**Illuminara**  
It was allowed to. That's the difference.

Prycé took the pencil from behind his ear. In the gallery the bent spoke stood where he had left it, and tonight he did not need to go down and read it. In the lamp of the radio shed he opened a pocket notebook, copied out the crest figure and the date beside it, and then, in the space where for eleven years he had written the careful word, wrote another.
*Holding.*

Illuminara stayed until the water began to fall, and by morning she was gone. The valley woke to a river running full and quiet, and the school bus came down past the terraces and stopped at the clinic, as it did every day.

critic_line: A dam assessor who hid a moving seam to save his valley chooses truth when Illuminara turns his strongest objection into an ordered repair, a resident-owned safety rule and a measurable storm test that keeps both the people and their livelihood standing.

translation_sl.title: OCENJEVALEC, KI JE OHRANIL JEZ
translation_sl.deck: Enajst let je na videz pošten mož podpisoval varnostno potrdilo, za katero je vedel, da je lažno, jez pa lahko popravijo le ljudje, ki jih je njegova laž skušala zaščititi.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v osmih tednih: številka, ki miruje, stik v temi, posojilo, prebrano zaradi datuma in vrat, ki jih nihče ni uporabil, cena vode, kreditni odbor, ki najprej prisluhne dolini, ter neurje, izmerjeno glede na vnaprej zapisano območje.

scenes.title: Številka, ki miruje
paragraphs: *Harrow Vale, pisarna uprave za vode · ponedeljek, 16:10 · šestinpetdeset dni pred sezono neurij*

Regionalna oblast jo je poslala preverit poplavni model doline in model je bil dober. Illuminara je v njem preživela dva dni, kakor ključavničar preživi popoldne v ključavnici. Padavine so imele razpon. Prst je imela razpon. Le en vhodni podatek je popolnoma miroval, in miroval je nad šest tisoč strehami.

**Illuminara**  
Levi opornik, blok enaintrideset. Enajst let meritev stika, ena na mesec. Gospod Prycé, voda v pobočju ne miruje tako spokojno. Vsak drug merilnik zatrepeta, ko dežuje po grebenu. Ta je gluh.

Dovan Prycé ji je postavil skodelico čaja ob komolec, preden je odgovoril. Imel je enainšestdeset let, bil je urejen in miren, človek, ki je vse življenje preživel kot najtišja oseba v prostorih, kjer so sprejemali odločitve.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Merilnik je star, stik pa suh. Temu bi rekel pohvala injektiranju. Harrow je dolgočasen jez, gospa Illuminara. Večina mojega dela je skrbno zapisovanje besede *zadovoljivo*.

Nekoč je bila sodna tolmačka in še vedno je prisluškovala stavkom, ki so bili vnaprej izurjeni. Ta je bil gladko obrušen. *Dolgočasen*, je rekel nežno, kakor človek, ki zapira vrata, ki jih je sam naoljil.

**Illuminara**  
Nikogar ne obtožujem. Sprašujem, kakšen bi moral biti jez, da bi bila ta serija poštena meritev. Rada bi ga videla. Nocoj, če mi posodite ključ galerije.
Premor je trajal manj kot pol sekunde. To ni bil strah. Bil je zvok človeka, ki se odloča, katero od dveh resnic bo ponudil najprej.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Svetloba je najboljša ob mraku. Vzemite modri ključ. Prišel bom za vami, ko zaklenem.
Ni pogledal proti polici za svojo pisalno mizo, kjer je na žeblju viselo kolesarsko kolo z eno manjkajočo napero. Opazila je, da ni pogledal.

scenes.title: Svinčnik na zidu
paragraphs: *Jez Harrow, galerija levega opornika, blok 31 · isti večer, 19:40*

Beton je zapis teže. Illuminara je položila dlan na steno galerije in jo brala kot sistem poti, po katerih potuje sila, ter nekaj mest, kjer se poti niso strinjale. Pri bloku enaintrideset se je razcepila pot, ki se ne bi smela. Obremenitev je drsela vstran skozi stik, ki ni bil debelejši od črte svinčnika, in stik pod njeno roko ni miroval.
*Razlaga*, si je rekla. *Ne dokaz. Preizkusi jo.*

Uradni merilnik razpoke, medeninasti kazalnik, prilepljen čez stik, je bil skupaj z lestvico prebarvan s svežo občinsko zeleno barvo. Ob njem, v višini kolena, je bilo na zid pripeto ravnilo, čez razpoko pa je kot kazalec segala upognjena kolesarska napera. Po ometu navzdol je tekla kolona črtic s svinčnikom, vsaka z datumom v drobni, skrbni pisavi. Brala jih je od spodaj. Devet let so napredovale za štiri desetinke milimetra na leto. Nato zadnji dve zimi vsakič za milimeter in pol. In potem na vrhu tri črtice v devetih dneh.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Našli ste mojo napero.

**Illuminara**  
Našla sem vaš svinčnik. To je najpoštenejši zapis v tej dolini.
Sedel je na boben za kable, kakor da so njegove noge nekaj sprejele pred njim.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Ob štirih desetinkah sem lahko živel ob njem. Zdaj vsako jutro pridem sem, preden se odpre pisarna, da pogledam, ali se je kazalec premaknil, in vsako jutro se odločim, da ne bom zapisal, kar kaže.

**Illuminara**  
Koliko časa po vaši presoji?

**Dovan Prycé**  
Takšen stik ne poči. Neha popuščati in na dan, ko neha, nima več česa popustiti. Še ena mokra jesen, povrh pa taljenje snega? Doline ne bi zastavil na drugo. Tudi na prvo ne.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj potem barva?
Enkrat se je zasmejal samemu sebi.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Pred enajstimi leti sem bil mlajši ocenjevalec. Stari Ketteridge je ob tem bloku na rob zapisal: *zahteva ukrepanje*. Aldermere je to prebral kot *nevarno*, ker ima njihova kreditna zaveza sprožilec in ta beseda ga je potegnila. Posojilo so odpoklicali v tridesetih dneh. Obrat so zaprli. Dva tisoč dvesto ljudi je odšlo v eni zimi in pomagal sem nalagati kombije. Na naslednjem potrdilu je bilo z mojo roko zapisano *zadovoljivo, ob spremljanju*, in odtlej spremljam. Vašo poštenost plačujejo hiše drugih ljudi. Pokažite mi popravilo, zaradi katerega nihče ne izgubi službe, ali pa priznajte, da boste nekoč storili, kar sem jaz, le z več pričami.
To je bil dober ugovor in Illuminara ni hitela mimo njega. Za njim je v temi galerije v odtoku kapljala voda, glasna kakor ura.

**Illuminara**  
Popravila nimam. Imam dve dejstvi, nobeno pa še ni razsodba: stik se premika in enajst let ste bili edini, ki je to vedel. Zato vam lahko obljubim tole, in tu se obljuba konča. Nocoj ne prijavim ničesar. Nič z vašim imenom ne zapusti te galerije in nič o jezu ne gre posojilodajalcu ali mestu, dokler ne obstaja načrt, v katerem je prostor tudi za vas. Toda stika ne bom prepustila vašemu svinčniku, niti svojemu. Sunniva Achterberg bo ob prvem svitu čez blok enaintrideset položila optični kabel, da se bova prepirala z meritvijo, ne z menoj. Berem silo, gospod Prycé, in lahko se motim. Najprej pa me poučite o denarju doline.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Dajte obljubi konec, pa vam dam številko. Voda na dolvodni strani tega bloka. Ali petnajst stotink milimetra čez razpoko v šestih urah. Tega se bojim od druge zime. Stik, ki naredi to, ne leze več.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je to meja in narisali ste jo vi, ne jaz. Dokler kabel ni dejaven, bova napero odčitavala vsako uro, izmenoma vi in jaz, vsako vrednost pa zapisala pod prejšnjo; ista meja velja za napero in za kabel. Če jo kabel prestopi ali če vidim vodo na tisti strani, je tedna konec v tisti uri. Pokličem regionalno številko za nujne primere, odpre se načrt evakuacije, vi pa to prvi slišite od mene. Kaj boste upravi povedali o enajstih letih, izberete sami. Ali bodo ljudje opozorjeni, če stik popusti, pa ne. Znotraj te meje vas prosim za en teden.
Upognjeno napero je prijel med dva prsta in nekaj časa gledal le svojo pisavo.

**Dovan Prycé**  
En teden. Pridite k meni. Veliko papirja imam.

scenes.title: Beseda in datum
paragraphs: *Prycéjeva kuhinja, Harrow Vale · ista noč, 01:20*

Posojilna pogodba je odprta ležala na kuhinjski mizi, kup debel kakor opeka, v robovih pa enajst let njegovih zapiskov s svinčnikom. Denarja doline jo je učil tako, kakor človek uči jezik, ki ga je moral govoriti sam. Pri členu štirinajst pika tri mu je glas otrdel.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Dogodek stanja jezu. Če pooblaščeni ocenjevalec razvrsti jez v razred D, nevaren, lahko posojilodajalec v tridesetih dneh odpokliče posojilo. To je vsa past. Ni pomembno, koliko stane popravilo. Pomembno je, da podpišem to besedo.
Past, je pomislila Illuminara, je narejena za eno določeno žival. Stavku je sledila do konca, kjer je odvisni člen ležal v lastni senci.

**Illuminara**  
*Razen če na datum takega potrdila že poteka program sanacije, ki ga je odobril inženir posojilodajalca.* Ste to prebrali?

**Dovan Prycé**  
Velikokrat. Da bi program odobrili, mora nekdo posojilodajalcu razkriti napako. To je zaklenjena soba, ključ pa je ista beseda.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo razkrije? Ne vi. Vi ste ocenjevalec; vi potrjujete. Razkrije posojilojemalec. Preberite mi štirinajst pika pet.
Obrnil se je k dodatkom na koncu in obstal pri enem, ki ga že leta ni odprl.

**Dovan Prycé**  
*Posojilojemalec lahko pisno obvesti o sumu stanja. Kreditni uradnik lahko odobri mirovanje do devetdeset dni, da inženir posojilodajalca pregleda program sanacije. Tako obvestilo ni potrdilo ali priznanje razvrstitve in nobena kršitev ni odpuščena.*
Pogledal je datum dodatka. Bil je iz zime po zaprtju Obrata.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Aldermere je ta vrata napisal sam, po kombijih. Naslovljena so na posojilojemalca, jaz pa nikoli nisem bil posojilojemalec, zato sem jih vložil med administrativno.

**Illuminara**  
Potem beseda nikoli ni bila ključ in nikoli ni bila ključavnica. Datum je. Člen štirinajst pika tri sprašuje, kaj se dogaja na dan, ko potrdite, ne kaj je bilo rečeno prej. Zato je zaporedje pomembnejše od poguma. Vossova da obvestilo po členu štirinajst pika pet. Halloran odobri mirovanje. Aldermerejev inženir odčita kabel in odobri program. Šele nato potrdite, niti uro prej. Če potrdite najprej, se izjema nikoli ne uporabi.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Do takrat pa se stik še naprej premika.
Obračal je strani. Direktor Obrata je lahko *zaradi pregleda, vzdrževanja ali varnosti* gladino zbiralnika znižal za največ dvanajst metrov, ne da bi kogar koli obvestil.

**Illuminara**  
Potisk na stik narašča s kvadratom globine. Harrow pri polnem bazenu drži osemintrideset metrov. Odvzemite enajst in potisk na blok enaintrideset bo približno polovičen. Znižanje ni program in posojilodajalec bi ga upravičeno zavrnil kot takega. Je pa tisto, kar ohrani stik živ v dneh, ki jih potrebuje papir.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Enajst metrov je triintrideset milijonov kubičnih metrov. Obrat bi svojo zalogo izlival po reki za nič.

**Illuminara**  
Ne za nič, če jo kdo dolvodno potrebuje. Komu jeseni manjka vode?

Odprl je usta, da bi rekel *nikomur*, pa jih spet zaprl. Terase: štiri tisoč hektarjev sadovnjakov in ozimne pšenice ter zunajtočne zbiralnike, ki jih je namakalna zveza Corrina Askeja vsako leto marca polnila po črpalni ceni.

**Illuminara**  
Naj torej iz nje odgrizne ceno. Praznjenje mora biti počasno, največ četrt metra na dan, sicer bodo mokra ramena doline zdrsnila v bazen. To je štiriinštirideset dni. Imate jih šestinpetdeset. Začnite v četrtek, sicer zmanjka računice, še preden zmanjka vode.
Prycé je nekaj časa tiho sedel. Zunaj je pes nekoga lajal v nič.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Izpustili ste najmočnejšo stvar proti sebi in opazil sem. Tudi če posojilodajalec dovoli program, sem enajstkrat potrdil *zadovoljivo*. To je napačno prikazovanje, samostojna kršitev ne glede na jez. Izjema varuje človeka, ki zamuja. Ne varuje lažnivca.

**Illuminara**  
Ne, ne varuje ga. Na to morate odgovoriti vi in jaz ne morem namesto vas. Toda vi ste tisti, ki mora ostati na nogah.

**Dovan Prycé**  
In ljudje spodaj?

**Illuminara**  
Kar veste, bodo slišali istega dne kot posojilodajalec, ostalo pa bodo slišali od vas, preden kdor koli razpravlja o vašem imenu.
Vsako uro, dokler ni posivelo jutro, je eden od njiju šel po stezi v galerijo, odčital upognjeno napero ob ravnilu in zapisal številko pod prejšnjo. Ni se premaknila.

scenes.title: Koliko je vredna voda
paragraphs: *Obrat Tarn, direktorjeva pisarna · sreda, 07:30*
Marguerite Voss je vsemu prisluhnila stoje in s plaščem še vedno na sebi, kar je bilo v Harrow Valu znamenje vljudnosti. Ko je Prycé končal, ni pogledala Illuminare. Pogledala je njega.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Enajst let sem podpisovala za jez, v katerega nisem mogla videti, na besedo človeka, ki sem mu zaupala šolo svojih otrok.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Da.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Na vašem stolu bi storila enako, zato lahko ta stol vržem v vas. Sami boste to povedali upravi, Dovan, s svojimi besedami, in ne boste se skrili za razpoko. To so moji pogoji. Sama bom podpisala vzdrževalni nalog za spodnje zapornice: ob zori v četrtek. In kot posojilojemalka bom podpisala obvestilo Aldermereju po členu štirinajst pika pet: sum stanja, neodvisno izmerjen, ocenjevalec pa bo v ponedeljek osebno podal svoj opis. Vašega imena ni na njem. Resnično je, ostalo pa morate povedati vi.

**Dovan Prycé**  
To je resničen stavek. Ostalo bom povedal.

Sunniva Achterberg je vso noč vozila z bobnom optičnega kabla v prtljažniku kombilimuzine in dan preživela leže na tleh galerije. Na mizo je položila izpis. Bil je znotraj meje, ki jo je Prycé narisal v galeriji, vendar ne daleč.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Nič cela enaintrideset milimetra čez blok enaintrideset v osemnajstih urah. To je hitreje od vašega svinčnika, gospod Prycé. Včeraj bi rekla dolgočasno. Danes bom rekla, da je to rep nečesa. Odvzemite enajst metrov in moj model vrne rezervo. Podpisala bom *varneje*, izmerjeno. Ne bom podpisala *varno*. Še nikoli nisem videla, da bi ta beseda preživela pomlad.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Voda plača tretjino prve faze: dvaindvajset sider v blokih od devetindvajset do triintrideset. Halloran lahko na svoj podpis sprosti prvi obrok do določene meje, prvo fazo pa sem ocenila pod njo. Obvestilo pride do Aldermereja ob devetih v četrtek, ob isti uri pa gre na vsa vrata v dolini obvestilo: stik, zniževanje bazena, javni sestanek v ponedeljek. Posojilodajalec ne bo slišal niti besede, ki je dolina ne bi.
Corrin Aske je opoldne prišel v škornjih in poslušal v tišini, ki je postajala vse nevarnejša.

**Corrin Aske**  
Hočete, da kupim vaš strah.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Hočem, da kupite triintrideset milijonov kubičnih metrov za terase po devet centov namesto devetnajstih, kolikor vas stane črpanje.

**Corrin Aske**  
Po devet. V mojih zbiralnikih do božiča, ne marca, s pisnim jamstvom, da je ne morete vzeti nazaj. In sedež v odboru za varnost jezu. Tudi moji ljudje spijo pod tistim zidom. Če hočete, da spim, kabel berem sam. Zanj ne izvem pozneje.

**Marguerite Voss**  
Dogovorjeno. Sedež in jamstvo.

**Corrin Aske**  
In on?

**Dovan Prycé**  
Za potrdila bom odgovarjal. Ne prosim vas, da vam je to všeč.

**Corrin Aske**  
Dobro. Ni mi.

scenes.title: Najprej prebivalci
paragraphs: *Mestna hiša Harrow, Aldermerejev kreditni odbor na zaslonu · naslednji ponedeljek, 15:00*

Teodor Halloran se je pojavil na zaslonu z natisnjenim dnevnim redom v roki, skrben človek s skrbno kravato. V četrtek je odobril mirovanje. Imre Dalca, Aldermerejev inženir, je petek preživel ob samostojnem branju Achterberginega kabla in tisto jutro ob devetih odobril prvo fazo programa. Dvorana je bila polna in Illuminara ni rekla ničesar.

**Teodor Halloran**  
To je kreditni pregled. Prva točka je skladnost s kreditnimi zavezami.

**Anneke Rowe**  
Prva točka sem jaz. Delam kot medicinska sestra na kliniki devetsto metrov pod vznožjem tega jezu, šola mojih sinov pa je na ravnici ob njem. Preden kdor koli govori o posojilu, mi povejte, ali lahko moji otroci spijo.

**Teodor Halloran**  
Gospa Rowe, z vsem spoštovanjem, to je posojilodajalčev—

**Anneke Rowe**  
Z vsem spoštovanjem, slišala bom najprej to ali pa ničesar.
Dovan Prycé je vstal. Njegovi zapiski so se enkrat zatresli, potem pa ne več. Enajst let je vadil, je pomislila Illuminara, pred ogledalom, ki ga ni nikoli videla.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Enajst let sem jez Harrow potrjeval kot *zadovoljiv, ob spremljanju*. Ni bil. Blok enaintrideset ima stik, ki se vsako zimo premika hitreje, in prikril sem hitrost. Od četrtka so bazen znižali za eno celo eno desetinko metra, neodvisni kabel pa kaže, da se je premikanje upočasnilo za petino. Gospod Dalca je odobril prvo fazo programa sanacije, zato ob treh kot pooblaščeni ocenjevalec jez Harrow razvrščam v razred D pri polnem bazenu. Gospa Rowe, ne bom vam rekel, da je šola varna. Poplavna enota Ilse Bram je v petek znova izračunala zemljevid porušitve. Pri polnem bazenu porušitev bloka enaintrideset pošlje na vašo ravnico štiri metre vode v enajstih minutah. Pri gladini, ki jo bomo ohranili do sezone neurij, približno pol metra v štiridesetih. To je drugačna poplava. Ni brez poplave. Če kabel pokaže več kot petnajst stotink milimetra v šestih urah ali če bazen preseže enaintrideset metrov, se sprožijo sirene in ravnica se izprazni, ne glede na nebo. Jaz sem razlog, da ste morali vprašati.
Anneke Rowe nekaj časa ni rekla ničesar.

**Anneke Rowe**  
Štirideset minut je želja, če imamo eno cesto in šeststo otrok. Ravnica se izprazni v petindvajsetih ali pa hočem drugo cesto. Klinika pa mora biti na radijskem omrežju isto uro kot galerija.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Radio lahko sam vključim v načrt. Štoparica pri sredinem preizkusu siren bo vaša.
Sedla je, kar je bila v tistem prostoru sodba zase.

**Anneke Rowe**  
V sredo, pod sireno pa bom stala sama. Nadaljujte. Njemu povejte ostalo.

**Teodor Halloran**  
Gospod Prycé, pravkar ste mi povedali, da ste ponaredili enajst potrdil, prvi vzgib mojega odbora pa bo odpoklic posojila. Moje mirovanje pokriva stanje. Ničesar ne odpušča. Odbor bo vprašal, ali je program na datum vašega potrdila že potekal in ali *odobren* pomeni *financiran*. Gospod Dalca je prvo fazo odobril ob devetih, jaz sem ob desetih na svoj podpis sprostil prvi obrok, vi pa ste potrdili ob treh. To zaporedje sem zapisal v zapisnik. Če bi potrdili v četrtek, bi vam zdaj govoril, da se izjema ni nikoli uporabila.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Vem. Moral sem čakati.
Halloran je prvič pogledal žensko, ki je sedela poleg ocenjevalca.

**Teodor Halloran**  
In vi ste?

**Illuminara**  
Nekdo, ki so ga poslali preverit poplavni model. Ena številka, če smem: če bi Aldermere danes odpoklical posojilo za jez s premikajočim se stikom, dolino, ki jo je treba evakuirati, in zaprt Obrat, koliko bi iztržili za zavarovanje?

**Teodor Halloran**  
Zelo malo.
Številko na svojem zaslonu je gledal dlje, kot gleda človek, ki se je že odločil.

**Teodor Halloran**  
Napačnega prikazovanja ne morem odpustiti; o tem odloča odbor. Lahko ga predložim ob še veljavnem mirovanju in s priporočilom, ki vključuje to številko. Posojilo bom evidentiral kot dejavno sanirano, ne kot nevarno. Potrdila gospoda Prycéja ostajajo pridržana, odbor bo odločil v devetdesetih dneh, jaz pa bi si poiskal odvetnika.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Imam jo. Njen nasvet bi moral upoštevati že pred leti.

scenes.title: Drži
paragraphs: *Jez Harrow, krona · devetinštirideset dni pozneje, 02:10*

Prvo neurje sezone je čez greben prišlo kakor na stežaj odprta vrata. Štiristo milimetrov v dveh dneh. Bazen se je ponoči dvignil za dve celi štiri desetinke metra, nad njim pa je bilo enajst metrov prazne doline. Dvaindvajset sider, zavrtanih v bloke od devetindvajset do triintrideset, je držalo stik v prijemu, kakršnega ni poznal, odkar je bil jez mlad.

Pred dežjem je Achterbergova na kartico zapisala tri vrstice in jo prilepila nad radio v galeriji. Ob dvigu za dve celi štiri desetinke metra naj bi se stik odprl za največ šest stotink milimetra. Za mejo, ki jo je Prycé narisal v galeriji, bi se oglasile sirene. Ob vsaki polni uri je Askejev nočni delavec po radiu glasno prebral meritev kabla. Do polnoči ena stotinka. Do ene dve. Do dveh tri.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Štiriinštirideset dni zniževanja. Obrat bo deset let nosil nov dolg. Enajst družin je odšlo od septembra; pravijo, da bi odšle v vsakem primeru, čeprav v tem nikoli nisem našel utehe. Enaintridesetega končam. Odbor me bo kaznoval in vzel mi bo licenco. Moja odvetnica pravi, da bom obdržal hišo.

**Illuminara**  
In gospa Rowe?

**Dovan Prycé**  
Fanta sta v ponedeljek šla v šolo na ravnici. V sredo je merila čas vaje s sirenami. Triindvajset minut. Pravi, da se ob treh še vedno zbuja. Rekel sem ji, da se tudi jaz, in rekla je: dobro.
Dež je udarjal po kroni. Pod njima je dolina ležala temna in neevakuirana, šest tisoč ljudi je spalo za zidom, ki je bil prvič v enajstih letih opisan resnično.
Ob treh je val dosegel vrh in iz galerije se je po radiu oglasil Achterbergin glas.

**Sunniva Achterberg (radio)**  
Vrh. Štiri stotinke. Znotraj območja. Celice sider so se dvignile z vodo, torej obremenitev nosijo sidra. Če bi to povzročil samo znižani bazen, ne bi pokazale ničesar. Varneje, izmerjeno. Besedo *varno* bom zapisala na kartico, ko bom videla, da preživi pomlad.

**Dovan Prycé**  
Premaknilo se je.

**Illuminara**  
Smelo se je. V tem je razlika.

Prycé je izza ušesa vzel svinčnik. V galeriji je upognjena napera stala tam, kjer jo je pustil, in nocoj mu ni bilo treba iti dol, da bi jo odčital. V svetlobi radijske lope je odprl žepno beležnico, prepisal vrednost ob vrhu in datum ob njej, nato pa v prostor, kamor je enajst let zapisoval previdno besedo, napisal drugo.
*Drži.*

Illuminara je ostala, dokler voda ni začela upadati, do jutra pa je odšla. Dolina se je zbudila ob polni in tihi reki, šolski avtobus pa je pripeljal mimo teras in ustavil pri kliniki, kakor vsak dan.

translation_sl.critic_line: Ocenjevalec jezu, ki je prikrival premikajoči se stik, da bi rešil svojo dolino, izbere resnico, ko Illuminara njegov najmočnejši ugovor spremeni v urejeno sanacijo, varnostno pravilo v lasti prebivalcev in merljiv preizkus v neurju, ki ohrani tako ljudi kot njihov način preživljanja.
